items.title: As the team grows, when does splitting into services start paying off?
items.description: L2's decision procedure names team count as the driver that dominates the other three. A monolith needs every pair of people to be able to coordinate about a shared codebase — communication paths grow as team_size × (team_size − 1) / 2. Splitting into services grouped ~4 people per team only requires coordination BETWEEN teams, not within them. Drag team size and watch where the modular line drops below the monolith line — that crossover, not a fixed headcount, is the point worth splitting at.
items.compute: const n = params.teamSize; const monolithOverhead = Math.round((n * (n - 1)) / 2); const teamsOfFour = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / 4)); const modularOverhead = Math.round((teamsOfFour * (teamsOfFour - 1)) / 2); return { monolithOverhead, modularOverhead };

outputs.label: Split into ~4-person teams: team-to-team coordination paths
